_about: Curated looks of Downtown Atlanta buildings, each from a cited source, matched to a footprint by position (`at` = [lat, lon], within `radius` m) and, where there are several, the tallest one. The pipeline's own data comes first (Overture, OSM tags, Wikidata); these fill what no feed has. `label` is for humans: it is never baked into a tile, and no name, brand or sign is drawn from this file. Fields: material (brick|glass|concrete|stone|metal|stucco|wood), colour and roofColour (#rrggbb, the colour of the material as it weathers), style (classical|victorian|artdeco|modernist|brutalist|postmodern|contemporary|vernacular), year, crown (m of crown above the last floor: no windows), roofMaterial.

entries.label: 191 Peachtree Tower
entries.src: Wikipedia: facade of flame-finished Rosa Dante granite, gray-tinted windows, a lit double crown; a Wikimedia Commons photo shows pale warm pink-beige granite, narrow tall windows between strong piers, two crowns

entries.label: Georgia-Pacific Tower
entries.src: Wikipedia: clad in pink granite from Marble Falls, Texas, stepped down to the street; OSM building:colour #ba9287; a Wikimedia Commons photo shows it darker (rose-brown) with a square window grid

entries.label: Westin Peachtree Plaza
entries.src: Wikipedia: a cylinder cast in reflective glass, about 5600 flat windows

entries.label: Truist Plaza
entries.src: Wikipedia: a postmodern square tower with an elaborate base and crown; a Wikimedia Commons photo shows a dark metal and glass grid wall, stepped crown and pinnacle

entries.label: Southern Bell Telephone Company Building
entries.src: Wikipedia: an austere Art Deco style, completed 1929 at six stories, 14 by 1963

entries.label: Richard B. Russell Federal Building
entries.src: Wikipedia: a 26-story International style building; a Wikimedia Commons photo shows pale grey-white precast concrete with deep horizontal strip windows

entries.label: Equitable Building
entries.src: Wikipedia: a typical International-style skyscraper by SOM, 1968

entries.label: Hurt Building
entries.src: Wikipedia: marble and glazed brick piers with terra cotta spandrels, a heavy decorative cornice; a Wikimedia Commons photo shows pale grey glazed brick, cream terra cotta spandrels and a white marble base

entries.label: William-Oliver Building
entries.src: Wikipedia: Atlanta's first completed Art Deco skyscraper, 1930

entries.label: Atlanta Central Library
entries.src: Wikipedia: Marcel Breuer, Brutalist, concrete facade, 1980

entries.label: Georgia State Capitol
entries.src: Wikipedia: Neoclassical, a four-story portico of stone piers; OSM building:material stone

entries.label: State Farm Arena
entries.src: Wikipedia: Cor-Ten weathering steel on the exterior

entries.label: Candler Building
entries.src: Wikipedia: Beaux-Arts, 1906, 17 stories; a light marble and terra cotta facade (colour approximate)

entries.label: Flatiron Building
entries.src: Wikipedia: English-American Building, completed 1897, 11 stories, a Chicago school design (steel frame, masonry skin)

entries.label: Atlanta City Hall
entries.src: Wikipedia: constructed 1930, a Neo-Gothic high-rise office tower; a Wikimedia Commons photo shows buff limestone with tall slender windows between vertical piers (drawn as vertical strips)

entries.label: Atlanta Marriott Marquis
entries.src: Wikipedia: Portman design, 1985, a bulging base; a Wikimedia Commons photo shows a flat tan-brown precast face with narrow strip windows
